A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although students who are more experienced with VPA are more successful at using inquiry skills, the novelty of the task is an important factor to consider when designing learning experiences.
, in general, students who had previous experience with VPA performed better in the new scenario than students who did not have prior experience.
prior experience can be a double-edged sword, as students may benefit from previous practice, yet may also be less motivated to learn new skills.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VPA system, which provides a flexible environment that allows students to engage in open-ended inquiry activities, can help to develop and transfer students’ inquiry skills.
the design of VPA scenarios needs to consider the balance between transferability and novelty, to support both learning of new skills and motivation.
